set.st: Treasure lists say wealthy farmer Thomas Fontaine, known to carry large sums, was murdered near Mentor in October 1904 and little money was found on him. The record says otherwise: the Grand Forks Herald of 21 Oct 1904 ('Fontaine Is Not Killed') found Phileas Fontaine alive, working at a meat market in East Grand Forks. The man murdered near Mentor about 17 Oct 1904, by his travelling companion, later held at Woonsocket, R.I., was Joseph Mongeon, a thresher and spruce-gum picker with a little threshing money. He had told people he carried considerable money; whatever he had went with the companion, and nothing was hidden. The treasure-list version names the wrong man.
